+A project gets a task when it contains files Oxlint can lint.
+The workspace root also needs a `package.json` and a `src` or `lib` directory, so a standalone workspace that keeps its sources elsewhere gets no root task.
+Documentation-only and non-JavaScript projects get no target, and giving one a config of its own doesn't change that.
A project's task skips the roots of any projects nested inside it, so Oxlint lints each file once, under the project that owns it.
+The inferred task uses the `@nx/oxlint:lint` executor, which runs in batch mode by default.
+When a command lints several projects, such as `nx run-many -t lint` or `nx affected -t lint`, Nx starts one Oxlint process for all of them instead of one per project.
+Oxlint is fast enough that starting it dominates the time to lint a project, so this brings `nx run-many -t lint` close to running `oxlint` once at the workspace root.
+Nx splits the Oxlint report by project, so every project has its own cache entry and `nx affected` still picks projects individually.
+A violation fails every project that lints its file, which by default is only the project that owns that file.
+A nested project owns its own files: the project that contains it never lints them.
+To lint each project in its own process instead, pass `--batch=false`.
+Options on the task and flags on the command line are forwarded to Oxlint, so `nx run-many -t lint --config a.json` runs Oxlint with `--config a.json`, once for the whole run.
+When the projects in a batch set different Oxlint options, the batch runs with the first project's options and Nx prints a warning.
+Lint such projects with `--batch=false` on every run to give each its own options.
+A batch caches each project's result, and a run with `--batch=false` reuses it until the project's inputs or options change.
+A path in a project's `args` is an Oxlint option too, so in a batch it applies only when the first project's options include it.
+To lint more paths in a project, add them to `lintFilePatterns`.
+Oxlint runs from the workspace root, so a path in a forwarded option is relative to it rather than to the project: a project with its own config writes `"config": "libs/a/oxlint.local.json"`.

+The exceptions are the options Nx interprets itself: `--max-warnings` and `--deny-warnings` decide each project's result from that project's diagnostics, `--silent` empties the output, and `--format` is rendered by Nx from the Oxlint JSON report.
+`default` matches the Oxlint terminal output, and switches to one line per diagnostic in CI or under an AI agent, as Oxlint does.

+The `@nx/oxlint:lint` executor runs Oxlint on a project. When several projects lint in one command, Nx batches them: one Oxlint process lints every project and each project still gets its own result, cache entry, and output. Pass `--batch=false` to lint each project in its own process.

+Options not listed in the schema are forwarded to Oxlint as CLI flags, so `nx run-many -t lint --config a.json` runs Oxlint with `--config a.json`, and the same holds for options set on the target. Oxlint runs from the workspace root, so a path in a forwarded option is workspace-relative rather than project-relative.

+In a batch, Oxlint uses the first project's flags for every project, and Nx warns when another project sets different ones. Each project still uses its own `--format`, `--silent`, `--max-warnings`, and `--deny-warnings`.
+Narrow what a project lints with `lintFilePatterns`. Paths are workspace-relative and `{projectRoot}` is interpolated.
+Fixer flags such as `--fix` pass through to Oxlint.

+`format` is rendered by Nx from the Oxlint JSON report, so the values are `default`, `agent`, `github`, and `json`. In CI and under an AI agent, `default` renders one line per diagnostic, as Oxlint itself does.
